To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most important risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke are: 1) elevated blood cholesterol, 2) high blood pressure, 3) smoking, 4) diabetes, and 5) physical inactivity.

the development of a comprehensive approach to cardiovascular disease prevention that is based on the best available scientific information and that can be used by healthcare professionals to guide their patients in the adoption of healthy lifestyles.
the development of new and better ways to diagnose, treat, and prevent disease.
the primary prevention of coronary heart disease (CHD).

the primary prevention of atherosclerotoric cardiovascular disease is feasible, cost-effective, and highly desirable for all persons.
